words.gloss: like the flowing black sand ripples

literal: I, having desired, she who resides, her honey-dripping tresses / of the wealth-possessing Cholas' Uraiyur's great riverbank / fine sand's black ripples spread out like / have beautiful curls, are fragrant and cool.
translation: The honey-dripping tresses of her whom I love and live with are like the dark, wavy lines of water-ripples on the fine sands of the great riverbank of Uraiyur, belonging to the wealthy Cholas. They have beautiful curls; they are fragrant and cool.
modern: நான் விரும்பி வாழ்கின்ற தலைவியின் தேன் சொட்டும் கூந்தல், வளம் பொருந்திய சோழர்களது உறந்தையின் பெரிய காவிரித் துறையிலுள்ள நுண்மையான மணலில் நீர் வடியும்போது ஏற்படும் கருமணல் வரிகளைப் போன்றது. அக்கூந்தல் அழகிய நெளிவுகளை உடையது; நறுமணமும் குளிர்ச்சியும் பொருந்தியது.
explanation: This poem is spoken by the hero in the Kuriñci tiṇai, expressing his deep love and admiration for the heroine's beauty. He describes her hair, which is fragrant and cool, comparing its dark, wavy texture to the natural patterns formed on the riverbank. Specifically, he likens her curls to the dark sand ripples left by receding water on the fine sands of the Kaveri river at Uraiyur, the prosperous capital of the Cholas. This vivid comparison of her hair to a famous, beautiful landscape highlights her exceptional grace and high status. The key words 'நயந்து' (lovingly), 'அறல்' (black sand ripples), and 'நறுந்தண்ணியவே' (fragrant and cool) emphasize the sensory richness of his love.
